cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has been telling believers one thing, LOUD and clear: God's Son is far greater than the angels. He just warned them not to drift away from what they've heard, and friend, I've zoned out on an oven timer before, so I'm LISTENING. Now he talks about the world to come, the one he's been writing about.

cards.question: The writer says God has put the world to come under the angels.

cards.text: Then he quotes Scripture that asks God a question: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?” Great question, and I asked something like it from the bottom of a junk drawer.
The quote keeps going: God made man a little lower than the angels and crowned him with glory and honor. Man gets a CROWN, and all I ever got was my name carved into my handle!

cards.question: In that quote, God crowns man with glory and honor. How much does He put under man's feet?

cards.text: The writer says that when God put all things under man, He left nothing outside his control. Then he takes a look around at how things are right now.

cards.question: The writer says that right now we can see everything under man's control.

cards.text: Everything under man's feet, and I've watched people lose a wrestling match to a fitted sheet. But the writer says we DO see Jesus, made a little lower than the angels and now crowned with glory and honor.

cards.question: The writer gives a reason Jesus is now crowned with glory and honor. What is it?
By the grace of God, Jesus tasted death for ___.

cards.text: Now the writer says God is bringing many sons to glory, and Jesus is the author of their salvation. And it was fitting for God to make Him perfect in one very particular way.

cards.question: How was it fitting for God to make Jesus, the author of their salvation, perfect?

cards.text: Now the writer looks at Jesus, the One who sanctifies, and at the people He sanctifies. Here comes the part that hits home, baker.

cards.question: The writer says the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family.
Because they're one family, Jesus is not ashamed to call them ___.

cards.text: Some folks will hide behind a pillar at the airport to dodge their own cousin, but Jesus is NOT ashamed to call them brothers. Then the writer quotes three lines as Jesus' own words, starting with this one.

cards.question: In the first line, who does Jesus say He will proclaim God's name to?

cards.text: Jesus also says, “I will sing Your praises in the assembly.” Then come the other two lines: “I will put My trust in Him.” and “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
Now, since the children have flesh and blood, Jesus shared in their humanity too. And the writer says exactly why.

cards.question: By His death, Jesus would destroy the one who holds the power of death, the ___.
Jesus also came to free people who were held in slavery all their lives. What were they slaves to?
The writer says it's the angels that Jesus helps.

cards.text: Not angels. He helps the descendants of Abraham, Israel's forefather, so He had to be made like His brothers in every way, to serve God and make atonement for the sins of the people.

cards.question: Being made like His brothers, Jesus could become a merciful and faithful ___ ___ in service to God.

cards.text: One more thing, baker, and it's a BIG one. Jesus Himself suffered when He was tempted.

cards.question: Because of what Jesus Himself suffered, who does the writer say He is able to help?

findings.problem: Card 4 says the writer quotes three lines and starts with the proclaim line. Card 6 then adds 'I will sing Your praises in the assembly' and then 'the other two lines.' That makes four lines, not three. The text gives three quotations (He says / And again / And once again), and the first quotation holds both the proclaim and sing lines. The count Papa Dorin points out doesn't hold up.

rule.text: **Noticing:** What he points out must be true.

findings.problem: This one story card packs in three separate quoted lines: the rest of the 2:12 quote and both quotes from 2:13. That's more than two beats, and the card is only quotations with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: This card carries three beats in one long sentence: He helps Abraham's descendants (2:16), He had to be made like His brothers in every way (2:17), and the purpose of serving God and making atonement (2:17).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has almost no humor. Card 4's airport line is the only joke. Cards 1, 6, 7, 11 and 13 read as plain narration or pleasant lines with no comic energy, so the stop doesn't sound like Papa Dorin.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The joke 'all I ever got was my name carved into my handle!' contradicts his backstory. He was renewed and given a whole cookie planet, and he treasures the name the Millers carved, since keeping it was the one thing he asked for. Saying it's all he ever got changes his story and sounds ungrateful.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.
